paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: what you do matters, and your father's last words can say so out loud. Jacob doesn't hand out the same blessing like free samples. He gives each son the one that fits, and the Bible says he blessed each one "with a suitable blessing" (Genesis 49:28). Reuben lost ground because of what he did (Genesis 49:4), and Simeon and Levi got a hard word about their anger (Genesis 49:7). I think that was a heavy room to sit in, so I won't joke about it.

But look at where the hope lands. Judah's brothers will praise him, and the scepter stays with him "until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his" (Genesis 49:8, 10). Then Joseph, who was attacked by archers, "steadied his bow," and his strong arms were "tempered by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob" (Genesis 49:23-24). Joseph didn't hold steady on his own strength, and neither do you. God's hands were on him, and that's why he stood.

And right in the middle of it all, Jacob stops and says, "I await Your salvation, O LORD" (Genesis 49:18). Everything he's saying to his sons hangs on that one line. He's not waiting on his sons to fix the family, he's waiting on the LORD. So here's what I want you to take to the oven today, baker: your choices count, and your hope rests on God, not on how well you've done. That's the kind of truth worth stamping on every cookie.
